While one's first comment may be that this game shares some similarity to Super Smash Bros., Brawlhalla has unique features that make it a great experience. First, all Legends share similar attacks in hand-to-hand combat. Second, there are weapon combinations unique to each Legend, as well as stat distribution, making every Legend one-of-a-kind.

If one were to download this game for free, there is only one limitation. You will not have access to every Legend in the game, and will be given a handful each week. While this helps to allow a player to find a Legend that they enjoy using, it makes it more difficult for them if they are stuck with hard-to-master Legends. However, if a player were to get enough Gold (which can easily be obtained from leveling up your character or playing matches), you can purchase a Legend that you enjoy using. Alternatively, purchasing the "All Legends" pack for $19.99 will give you the full experience immediately, and will support the developers.

As for art style, each Legend has a unique design, even with similar color schemes. You can definitely figure out who is who in the middle of a battle. Each battlefield has unique designs, from simple to complex. Overall, if you are looking for a free alternative to Smash Bros., or you want to play a game with friends, whether online or not, this game is a great choice.

Brawlhalla is a fantastic brawler that offers endless fun, whether you're playing casually with friends or diving into competitive matches. Its roster of diverse characters and ever-evolving gameplay keeps things fresh, while the cross-platform support makes it easy to team up with or battle players on any device. The fast-paced combat feels satisfying, with each weapon adding its own layer of strategy and chaos.

That said, the game isn’t without its flaws. The free-to-play model is generous, but unlocking all characters can take a while unless you're willing to spend some money. Also, the matchmaking can occasionally feel unbalanced, especially for newcomers.

Overall, Brawlhalla is an addictive and accessible game that strikes a great balance between skill and fun. It’s easy to jump into but offers enough depth to keep you coming back for more.

Brawlhalla is the gaming equivalent of making a deal with the Devil, except you’re the one getting screwed by the fine print.

You boot it up thinking, “Just one game.”
Then one game becomes ten.
Ten becomes an evening.
And eventually you realize you've spent hours being launched into the sky by the same three attacks, wondering why you keep coming back.

The worst part is that you can’t leave.

You can uninstall it. You can swear it off. You can tell yourself you've finally broken free. But somehow, days later, there it is again—quietly waiting. And you return, because Brawlhalla has learned exactly how to make you miserable in a way that keeps you playing.

It doesn't want your money. It wants your soul.

Every victory feels like a brief moment of freedom. Every loss feels like the Devil reminding you who owns the contract. And somewhere between the rage, the matchmaking, and the desperate “one more game,” you realize the truth:

I never won the deal. I only agreed to keep playing.

10/10. I hate this game.
